title: PNP: No formal report yet on alleged threat reported by Sara Duterte's camp
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said Tuesday it has not received any formal report regarding an alleged threat against a former household helper of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said Tuesday it has not received any formal report regarding an alleged threat against a former household helper of Vice President Sara Duterte.

PNP spokesperson Police Brigadier General Allen Rae Co was asked about the claims of Duterte's lawyer Paolo Panelo that the household staff asked the vice president for help as she was allegedly being held against her will and was being forced to sign a document.
"Have they reported it to us? To the Philippine National Police? As of this time, we have received no reports that they have reported it to us," Co said at a press briefing.
Co pointed out that the PNP could not initiate an investigation based solely on social media posts containing unverified allegations.
He encouraged the vice president or anyone with information about the alleged threat to report the matter directly to the PNP.

According to a Facebook post by Atty. Paolo Panelo, Duterte's spokesperson, the vice president received a message at 11:19 p.m. on Monday "from what appeared to be the account of a former household staff member" asking for help and rescue in Manila.

The sender claimed to be under the custody or control of certain individuals who allegedly threatened their life. The former staff member also said they were being forced to sign a document but refused to do so.
Panelo said the person's whereabouts remain unknown and their safety and well-being have yet to be verified.

Panelo expressed concern that the incident could be part of what he described as a campaign by the Marcos administration to allegedly harass and coerce individuals into becoming false witnesses against Duterte amid her impeachment trial.
For its part, Malacañang said authorities should investigate the matter to determine the truth behind the Duterte camp's claims.

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro shrugged off Panelo's statement that the alleged incident may be part of the administration's supposed campaign against Marcos, saying the President was busy with the ongoing 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits. — VDV, GMA News
